entries.title: Jeremiah 12:1
segments: God does not forbid us to plead with him concerning his dealings, if it be done in the spirit of deep reverence and childlike confidence.

entries.title: Jeremiah 12:3
segments: When we are tempted to envy the wicked for their prosperity, we should look beyond present appearances and consider their latter end.

entries.title: Jeremiah 12:5
segments: If thou hast run--the swelling of Jordan; Jehovah's answer to the prophet, rebuking his impatience, and bidding him prepare for severer trials.  "The swelling of Jordan," is literally, "the pride of Jordan." Whether we understand this of its swollen flood, which the traveller is compelled to ford, or of the thickets which line its banks and are the habitation of wild beasts,

, it is a figure for great difficulties and dangers. 
 
It does not become those whom God has commissioned to preach his word, to faint and be discouraged on account of the persecutions which they endure for the truth's sake.  Rather should they make their present trials the occasion of fortifying themselves for trials in the future.

entries.title: Jeremiah 12:6
segments:
Even thy brethren; the men of Anathoth.  If even they have dealt treacherously with thee, prepare to enocunter still greater trials from the rulers of Jerusalem. 
 
In all ages of the world, the wickedness of the human heart has often overcome the closest ties of blood, so that the bitterest foes of the servant of God have been they of his own household.

entries.title: Jeremiah 12:9
segments:
A speckled bird; a bird of prey with varigated colors, which is an object of hatred and persecution to the other birds. 
 
  Come ye; a call to the nations to destroy Jerusalem.

entries.title: Jeremiah 12:10
segments: Pastors; here heathen rulers, the same as "spoilers,"

entries.title: Jeremiah 12:13
segments:
They have sown; that is, the Jews.  These words describe the disappointment of all their hopes, especially their trust on alliances with the heathen. 
 
  Your revenues; the result of your vain endeavors.

entries.title: Jeremiah 12:14
segments:
Mine evil neighbors; Jehovah calls the surrounding heathen nations his neighbors, because his dwelling-place was in Jerusalem. 
 
  I will pluck them out of their land; by causing them to be carried into captivity. 
 
  From among them; from being among them: I will remove my people from the midst of these nations to Babylon.  The captivity of Judah was followed by that of the surrounding nations that had hated and persecuted her. 
 
Though God employs wicked men as the instruments of chastising his people, he will in the end remember and punish their iniquities.

entries.title: Jeremiah 12:16
segments:
If they; these heathen nations. 
 
  Learn the ways of my people; become proselytes to their religion.
